_what_this_is: Authored. Which page each ruling belongs to. The ruling's own wording is recorded so the generator can FIND it in the source document without trusting a line number - if the wording no longer matches, the build report says so rather than emitting a link to the wrong place.

rulings.title: City-states are their painted metro regions on the cultural map. New Jersey, Delaware and Rhode Island cease to exist; Boston takes southern New Hampshire
rulings.not_built: Not built. No city-state exists, and New Jersey, Delaware and Rhode Island are ordinary nations on today's 61-nation board (DESIGN.md §2.1).

rulings.title: Iowa is in the Farmers Union
rulings.not_built: Not built — there is no Farmers Union nation. 'The Farmers Union' exists only as a movement in data/parties.json (read this session).

rulings.title: Colorado becomes the Front Range Republic; the Navajo Nation is trimmed to the Four Corners and the ground around it opens wanting in — Deseret's mechanism generalised
rulings.superseded_by: Narrowed by ruling 25 (line 908), which fixes the Navajo trim at roughly ten reservation Areas. Ruling 25 says explicitly 'This keeps ruling 3 intact' (line 913), so it refines rather than reverses.
rulings.not_built: Not built — neither the Front Range Republic nor the Navajo Nation exists on the board.

rulings.title: The Deep South is one nation as written, counterbalanced by separatist movements inside it
rulings.superseded_by: The counterbalance half was answered by ruling 28 (line 1064) and then settled by ruling 51 (line 1508): the balancing movements are ordinary movements whose homelands were painted across a state line, not a new category. The one-nation half stands.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Deep South nation exists.

rulings.title: Appalachia is the painted Southern Appalachia region, all 75 Areas — Knoxville, Chattanooga, eastern Kentucky and the western Carolinas included
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Appalachia nation exists. The 75 painted Areas are a cultural region, not a country.

rulings.title: The Gulf nation stops at the Tennessee line — Memphis stays in the Deep South, Cairo with the Farmers Union — so no one owns the whole river
rulings.superseded_by: Renamed by ruling 29 (line 1071): the Gulf nation becomes the Gulf Compact. The border itself is unchanged.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Gulf nation exists.

rulings.title: The Gullah coast goes whole to the Carolinas; the Deep South opens without a seaport
rulings.not_built: Not built — neither nation exists. Ruling 30's original fallback would have undone this ruling's landlocked giant, which is why that fallback was amended at lines 1079–1090.

rulings.title: Central Florida is the painted region — the Georgia line to Miami
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Central Florida nation exists.

rulings.title: The United States of New England; Rochester-and-Buffalo takes Clinton and the Franklin–Essex–Hamilton Area; alliance and free-trade deal pre-signed
rulings.superseded_by: Confirmed rather than changed by ruling 22 (line 870): 'Ruling 9 stands and nothing on the map moves.'
rulings.not_built: Not built — no United States of New England and no Rochester-and-Buffalo. There is also no treaty object of any kind in the game (DESIGN.md §12, 'No treaties and no aid'), so a pre-signed alliance has nothing to be stored in.

rulings.title: Superior is the Upper Peninsula plus the top of the Lower Peninsula — Michigan ground only
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Superior nation exists, and the document notes the painted Superior region is the wrong ground entirely (WI 6, MI 4, MN 2, line 1044). The Lower Peninsula line is one of the five still to be drawn.

rulings.title: When. Texas declared about two years before the game opens — spring 2034 — with its bicentenary as the deadline it set itself
rulings.not_built: Half built. The 1 March 2036 opening is real (js/calendar.js:6 and js/tunables.js:27–29). The spring 2034 declaration and 'every war in it has been fought' are not: nothing in the game carries a break-up date, and DESIGN.md §2.1 writes the shattering deliberately with no dated memories, so no grudge is eight turns fresh.

rulings.title: every nation spawns in every game; what rolls is its size.
rulings.not_built: Not built — nations do not roll at all. The board is authored in content/scenario-shattered.json and only Deseret's extent rolls (DESIGN.md §2.1). Six movements are deterministic and the other twenty-six roll a spawn chance, which is the opposite half of this ruling.

rulings.title: "doing well" is quality of life, influence and authority.
rulings.not_built: Not built, and the document says so at lines 713–716: every grievance term reads the holding nation only; nothing reads the nation a region would join. Finding C (lines 439–444) also warns that this ruling makes a badly-rolled nation's movement grow slower, which is one of three mechanisms all amplifying the same dice — the first thing a tuning pass must look at.

rulings.title: growing movements roll at the start on Deseret's shape, and new ones arise in play.
rulings.not_built: Not built — all thirty-two movements spawn once at setup and nothing founds a movement in play (DESIGN.md §7; the document states it at line 729).

rulings.title: the dice roll before the player chooses.
a realised movement's own ground is loyalty, not pressure.
rulings.not_built: Not built, and the code actively contradicts it. Read this session: js/game.js:1589 `hostility()` takes the largest movement share in an Area with no check on whose movement it is, and js/sentiment.js and js/ai.js do the same — so a nation is charged three times over for its own founding population. Logged as docs/deferred.md #14. Finding E (line 453) settles that loyalty reads the movement's share in an Area, not mere homeland membership.

rulings.title: a realised movement's homeland widens to its nation's founding ground, automatically.
rulings.not_built: Not built — nothing widens a realised movement's homeland; homelands come from data/parties.json exactly as baked. Without it, the document measures at lines 761–766 that Appalachia would hold 31 Areas its own movement cannot organise on, the Front Range Republic 31 and El Paso 14.

rulings.title: a reunification movement declares a winner, not a country.
rulings.not_built: Not built — a reunification-typed movement declares like any other and would found a sixth Texas out of whichever successor holds its core (doc lines 523–528).

rulings.title: reunification movements exist at several scales, and are contests between claimants.
rulings.superseded_by: Two of its four rows were corrected on 9 September at lines 829–836, with the ruling itself left unchanged. Row 4's claimant list was cut to three by ruling 20 the same day (Boston removed), so the table as printed still shows four and must be read against ruling 20. Row 2's 'five Californian successors' are named by round 2's ruling 32 — Los Angeles, the Bay Area, Riverside, SoCal and Northern California — which also puts Cascadia outside the contest, and the map actually breaks California into six pieces.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no reunification contest exists in js/.

rulings.title: the capital contest is Washington D.C., Philadelphia and New York City. Boston is out.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no capital contest exists. The 'Reunification of the Union' victory in js/victory.js:217 counts seats of government, half the people and half the economy, and knows nothing of claimants. The historical dates in the ruling are flagged in the document as from memory and unverified.

rulings.title: a nation can fund a movement, and it is a standing commitment rather than a move.
rulings.not_built: Not built — every movement record carries a `sponsor` field commented 'M6: a nation backing it' (js/movements.js:184) and no code reads or writes it. It is saved and restored and nothing else.

rulings.title: Boston stays inside the United States of New England; it is simply not a claimant.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no United States of New England exists.

rulings.title: the Four Corners is settled three ways, and the leftovers are rolled.
rulings.not_built: Not built — none of the three claimants exists as drawn, and nothing in js/ assigns contested counties by weighted dice.

rulings.title: a realised nation spreads outward at setup, in four rings of decaying odds.
rulings.superseded_by: SUPERSEDED by ruling 26 (line 1004): 'This replaces the ring ladder of ruling 24 as the way a nation's setup extent is decided.' The reason is given in the same paragraph — rings are geography-blind — and S77 at lines 972–993 had already measured the ladder amplifying the dice into a roughly sixfold range on Deseret, 12 to 77 Areas. Do not present the 33/11/3.7/1 ladder as live.
rulings.not_built: Not built and now superseded — nothing in js/ spreads a nation outward in rings.

rulings.title: the Navajo Nation is the reservation, not the painted region.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Navajo Nation exists on the board, and the document flags its own geography as 'from memory and unverified', wanting a check against a real reservation boundary before anything is built on it.

rulings.title: homelands are painted, not derived.
rulings.not_built: Not built — the editor authors 3-tier region hierarchies in which each Area belongs to at most one path (DESIGN.md §10). This ruling needs every Area to carry a list of claims with a level on each, which the document flags as architecture's problem at lines 1009–1013.

rulings.title: the four Type A nations get no movement built into them.
rulings.not_built: Not built — none of the four nations exists (the Carolinas, the Deep South, Central Florida, the Allegheny Republic).

rulings.title: the Deep South is balanced by rising movements that cross state lines.
rulings.superseded_by: Settled by ruling 51 (line 1508): 'This settles the Deep South counterbalance (ruling 28) without a new category.' Movements that cross borders are not a special kind — they are ordinary movements whose homeland was painted across a state line.
rulings.not_built: Deferred by Aaron inside the ruling itself — 'To be designed later in this round' (line 1069) — and then answered by ruling 51 rather than designed. Nothing built.

rulings.title: the two names are adopted: the Gulf Compact and the Allegheny Republic.
rulings.not_built: Not built — neither nation exists, so neither name appears anywhere in data/ or js/ (checked this session).

rulings.title: Central Florida gets no movement, and the Floribama leftovers go to it.
rulings.superseded_by: Amended in the same section at lines 1079–1090, on a measurement taken the same day: of Floribama's 21 Areas only Taylor County touches Central Florida and thirteen touch the Deep South, so the fallback as written would have handed the giant Mobile and Biloxi and undone ruling 7. The Gulf Compact's core now includes the Mississippi and Alabama Gulf counties and never rolls for them; the largest-neighbour fallback survives only as a general safety net.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Central Florida, Gulf Compact or Deep South nation exists.

rulings.title: four or five fragments painted per region, and the dice decide how many have coalesced.
rulings.not_built: Not built — there is no tier-3 concept anywhere in js/ (searched this session: the only 'stateless' matches are unrelated comments in power.js and tunables.js). Finding B (line 432) warns that if fragments have no stocks, grievance has nothing to read and the central mechanic of the game cannot happen on roughly 176 Areas.

rulings.title: stateless ground is no harder to take and dearer to hold.
rulings.superseded_by: Its premise is dropped by ruling 38 (line 1248) — 'Ruling 32's blanket premise is dropped' — after S83 measured the six stateless regions at a median armed share of 44.6% against 46.9% everywhere else, very slightly lower. The 'dearer to hold' mechanism survives through rulings 33 and 34; the claim that stateless ground is uniformly dear does not.
rulings.not_built: Not built. The document also records at lines 1113–1118 that the existing mechanism runs backwards for this: occupation upkeep scales with hostility, computed purely from organised movement membership, so ground with no movement is today the cheapest on the continent to occupy.

rulings.title: "resists being governed" is general, painted everywhere, heaviest on the six.
rulings.not_built: Not built — there is no per-Area 'resists being governed' property. Occupation upkeep reads js/game.js:1589 `hostility()`, which is purely the largest organised movement share.

rulings.title: resistance is capacity times willingness, and willingness is ideological.
rulings.not_built: Half built. The willingness term is the existing affinity function that civil liberties already uses (DESIGN.md §3.1), so nothing new is needed for it. The capacity term does not exist: measured this session, data/areas.json carries no armed-share field at all.

rulings.title: how the armed share is estimated.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no apportionment runs in build/ and no armed-share column exists in any file in data/. The 0.60/0.40/0.30 weights are Aaron's rounding of a Pew citation the document states has not been verified by that session (lines 1143–1146).

rulings.title: the source is RAND, pulled once and baked, never fetched at runtime.
rulings.superseded_by: Its description of the dataset is superseded at line 1193 by a reading of the file itself: 'RAND State-Level Firearm Ownership Database', version 1.0, 1 April 2020, 1,850 rows, 50 states, 1980–2016. The ruling's substance — RAND, pulled once, baked, never fetched at runtime — is unchanged.
rulings.not_built: Not built. Listed this session, build/raw/ holds CAGDP2.zip, co-est2024-alldata.csv, county_adjacency.txt, election2024_counties.csv and two subfolders, and no firearm file. Line 1188 says Aaron downloaded the workbook by hand for the design session; it never reached the repository, so the bake has no input.

rulings.title: the District of Columbia is assigned 6%, by hand, badged as an estimate.
rulings.not_built: Not built — there is no armed-share data in data/ for the figure to sit in. The ruling itself insists the number is invented and must never be presented as a RAND figure.

rulings.title: the stateless regions are not uniformly hard to hold; the data decides.
rulings.not_built: Not built — neither the stateless tier nor the armed-share data exists, so nothing yet makes Wyoming's fragments cost a conqueror more than Ohio's.

rulings.title: every movement has a VERB, and there are six.
rulings.not_built: Not built — measured this session: not one of the 32 records in data/parties.json carries a `verb` field. The old `type` field still drives behaviour and every movement, on crossing the line, declares independence.

rulings.title: the old types become ADJECTIVES, not behaviours.
rulings.not_built: Not built — measured this session: `type` is still a behaviour field holding autonomist, economic, ideological, indigenous, irredentist, reunification, separatist and theocratic-separatist, and no `adjective` field exists anywhere in data/parties.json.

rulings.title: Aaron's own extension, parked deliberately: a Deseret that shatters can grow a Deseret Reunify movement, if whoever holds the pieces governs them badly.
rulings.not_built: Parked by Aaron inside the ruling itself — 'Saved for later; the focus now is Texas, California and the eastern cities competing to restore the USA.' Nothing to build yet.

rulings.title: three of the six verbs are born in play, not painted.
rulings.superseded_by: Refined by ruling 44 (line 1376): 'that refines ruling 42 rather than contradicting it.' Expand and Reconquer still arise from a condition, but a condition can already be true on turn 0, so those two verbs can also be authored at setup.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no verbs exist, and nothing founds a movement during a game (DESIGN.md §7).

rulings.title: a movement is what people want; politics is how they get it.
rulings.not_built: Not built — a movement simply HAS an ideology (DESIGN.md §7.1), and that ideology is the multiplicative gate on where it can grow rather than the vehicle a separate want travels through. The gate-or-modifier question is parked by Aaron at lines 1586–1593.

rulings.title: four verbs changed.
rulings.not_built: Not built — measured in data/parties.json this session: Front Range Republic is still `separatist`, Hawaiian Sovereignty `indigenous`, and Blue-Collar Populist and Christian Nationalism both `ideological`. None of the four changes has been made.

rulings.title: six struck, and they split two ways.
rulings.not_built: Not built — measured this session: all six struck movements are still live in data/parties.json (Libertarians, Anarcho-Capitalist, Eastern Progressives, Techno-Autocrat, Delmarva Republic, Fifty-First State), and the file still holds 32 entries.

rulings.title: Canadian Refuge goes to the ideas file as F16.
rulings.not_built: Withdrawn by Aaron in the same entry he added it — 'A little too much for now' — and filed to the ideas file as F16. Nothing to build, and it must not be presented as a live movement.

rulings.title: a movement approaches a nation; the nation does not simply choose.
rulings.not_built: Not built — there is no petition machinery anywhere in js/. Finding A (line 426) also records that the petition threshold must sit below the secession threshold and nobody set one: if they are the same number no movement ever petitions, because it declares first.

rulings.title: several nations can be petitioned, and they compete for it.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no petition and no contest for one exists in js/.

rulings.title: refusing costs nothing immediately and everything eventually.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no standing offer and no clock. The `betrayed` relation memory the ruling points at does exist (js/relations.js) for a related injury.

rulings.title: petitions and everything like them belong to diplomacy.
rulings.not_built: An ownership ruling with nothing to build here — it moves the mechanism to round 5, docs/design/diplomacy-ideation.md, along with the alliance, vassal and bloc questions.

rulings.title: a movement is bound to counties, never to state lines.
rulings.not_built: Half built. Homelands are already stored per Area, but the document measures at lines 1515–1522 that roughly fifteen of the thirty-two are generated from state lists in build/build_parties.py, eight of which span several states, so their edges follow state lines nobody chose. The map editor of ruling 26 is the named fix and it is not built either.

rulings.title: the New Confederacy keeps its name for now, and it is marked for change.
rulings.not_built: Nothing to build — the name stands, and 'New Confederacy' is in data/parties.json today (verified). The ruling is a warning, and the wiki should carry it: 'Not renamed today; do not let this quietly become the final name.'

rulings.title: the Lakota Nation is Butte, Brown and Pennington: 3 Areas, about 271,000 people, and it holds Rapid City.
rulings.not_built: Not built — no Lakota Nation exists, and there is no Lakota movement in data/parties.json either (the register's nearest entry is the Native American Confederation). S100 at lines 1544–1553 records the underlying data finding: no combination of Areas is the Lakota nation and not also several white towns.

rulings.title: This is not a war game, and the arrows point the other way.
rulings.not_built: A frame, not a mechanic — nothing to build. Recorded as D181; quoted in full at line 31.

rulings.title: A war is a standing state, and it is one of seven.
rulings.superseded_by: Amended by ruling 17 (line 1132), which adds Wary. Said in as many words at line 117: 'Ruling 2 said seven states and named five live ones. Ruling 17 makes it six live states and eight in total. Everything below written before 9 September says "five states"; read it as six.'
rulings.not_built: No state between two nations exists in js/. Searching js/ for cease-fire, peace-treaty, hostile and wary returns one hit — a sentiment label at js/relations.js:171. Verified this session.

rulings.title: a cease-fire is temporary and carries a set number of turns.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. What happens at the expiry it defines is rewritten by rulings 33, 34, 35 and 36; the fixed term itself then becomes load-bearing for ruling 36, because a turn you did not choose must not cost you your action.
rulings.not_built: No cease-fire in js/.

rulings.title: what puts two nations into Hostile.
rulings.superseded_by: Cause 5 is bounded by ruling 37 (one hop, line 2398) and reshaped by ruling 38 (line 2491). C133 at line 2515 then derives that cause 5 must be an EVENT that fires once, structurally unlike causes 1–4, which are conditions that hold the clock back while they are live.
rulings.not_built: No hostile state in js/, so none of the five causes can fire. Cause 3 additionally depends on two things the economy does not do — desperation biting, and a settable price — both recorded as blocking on round 4 at lines 755–762.

rulings.title: a state is shared, not one-sided.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. The one-sided version is filed as F18 (line 781). It is re-used as the deciding argument in ruling 37's trace at line 2469.
rulings.not_built: No shared state object in js/. The directed decaying relations list that ruling 5 deliberately leaves alone IS built, and DESIGN.md §6.5 is explicit that making it symmetric 'would delete the rivalry'.

rulings.title: a war ends only by agreement, and refusing is allowed.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. The risk it recorded — a player held in a war they cannot leave by an opponent willing to bleed — is closed by ruling 15 at line 1116 (the stubborn opponent's own electorate removes them), and ruling 33 at line 2300 makes refusal more expressive by forcing the refuser to table terms nobody would accept.
rulings.not_built: No war and no agreement to end one in js/.

rulings.title: every state has an exit, and three of the four are clocks.
rulings.superseded_by: Amended by ruling 17 INSIDE ruling 7's own table — line 818 reads 'Hostile | time | ~~Peace~~ Wary (ruling 17)', with two new Wary rows added. The cease-fire row is then rewritten by ruling 8, whose first half ruling 33 supersedes at line 2253. Plain strikethrough is the only marker on the Hostile row, so it is easy to miss.
rulings.not_built: No state machine in js/.

rulings.title: a cease-fire ends in a negotiation, and its default is Hostile rather than War.
rulings.superseded_by: PARTLY SUPERSEDED, and the wiki must not present it whole. Line 2253: 'This supersedes the first half of ruling 8' — ruling 33 replaces the card that ASKED each side to send a treaty with a compulsory submission on a fixed turn. Ruling 34 (line 2309) then removes the counter-offer that extended the cease-fire. What survives untouched is the default: nothing signed means Hostile, not War (restated at line 2321).
rulings.not_built: No cease-fire in js/. The negotiation card it reuses is built for trade and transit only (DESIGN.md §6.7 'Negotiating', line 1191).

rulings.title: what Hostile costs.
rulings.superseded_by: Cost 3 — a hostile neighbour's matching movements grow faster inside you — is switched OFF ENTIRELY, not reduced, the moment a pair steps down to Wary: ruling 40, line 2564, 'Ruling 9's third cost of Hostile is switched off entirely the moment a pair steps down to Wary.' Costs 1, 2 and 4 apply in Wary at a fraction. Ruling 39 (line 2526) also replaced the four-scaled-costs shape with one acceptance multiplier.
rulings.not_built: None of the four costs exists in js/, because the state that would charge them does not. The corridor tolls they would raise are built (js/transit.js; transit.noticeTurns = 4 at js/tunables.js:814).

rulings.title: ground changes hands at the settlement, not turn by turn.
rulings.superseded_by: Refined by ruling 13 at line 1027: 'This refines ruling 10 rather than contradicting it, and the refinement is the good part.' What changes at the settlement is not the BORDER but the TENURE — the map moves when you win the roll, and the treaty launders occupied-war into occupied. Ruling 10's recorded cost, that a war with no visible front is hard to read, is answered by C79 at line 1043: the front is the pale part of your own country.
rulings.not_built: No war, no front and no settlement in js/.

rulings.title: war must be simple at the level the player touches it.
rulings.not_built: Consistent with what is built rather than missing from it. js/military.js opens 'NO UNIT COUNTERS, no stacks, no map tokens' and js/military.js:42 fixes the allocation at three roles. This ruling is a constraint on every other ruling in the round, not a thing to build.

rulings.title: how a fight resolves.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. The question it left open — what losing costs — is answered by ruling 14 (line 1059) and extended by ruling 23 (line 1652).
rulings.not_built: Partial, and the gap is the round's centre. The Field-vs-Border comparison exists (js/military.js:234–237) but the annex move rolls CivilWar.resolve (js/moves.js:1180), not a fight — so the defender is consulted only as a multiplier on the attacker's own civil-war score. §1a at line 82 states this and calls it 'the thing that is actually missing'. The structural change the ruling needs is that it must fire on EVERY attack.

rulings.title: ground you take is yours immediately, but it is held under a flag, and there are three flags.
rulings.superseded_by: Extended by ruling 26 (line 1818), which adds the fourth rung the three flags stopped short of — occupied ground eventually becomes ordinary ground. C81 at line 1053 records that ruling 13 alone left held ground 'still carrying some negative outcomes', permanently.
rulings.not_built: No occupied-war / occupied / occupied-movement flag exists anywhere in js/ — grepped this session, zero hits. The transit prohibition it invents would be a fourth reason in a broken-route explanation list that is already built (DESIGN.md §6.7). The 50% threshold it names is an invented placeholder and the document flags that it sits above the 0.40 secession threshold, so every occupied-movement Area is ground that was coming to you anyway (C80, line 1049).

rulings.title: an attack has two outcomes, and failure costs what you already spent.
rulings.superseded_by: Refined by ruling 23 (line 1652), stated at line 1670: 'It refines ruling 14 and the refinement is worth stating. Under ruling 23 a failed attack is no longer nothing.' A 30% attack is not 70% wasted — it is 30% conquest and 100% denial. C78's proposed readiness penalty is superseded (§8 q11, line 2860).
rulings.not_built: The premise IS built and verified: the price of an attack is debited before the roll, per Area and per head (annex.costPerArea = $250M at js/tunables.js:963, annex.costPopScale = $400 at :968). The two-outcome fight it prices is not.

rulings.title: what goes in a peace treaty, and what refusing one costs.
rulings.superseded_by: The 1.25× basis, flagged ambiguous at line 1093 ('needs one word settling and it is a number, so it is flagged rather than guessed'), is settled by ruling 22 (line 1569) — neither the winner's costs nor the loser's, but the PROPOSER's. The four levers and the 'refusing is not free' half stand unchanged.
rulings.not_built: No peace treaty object in js/. The two mechanisms 'bad things happening' relies on ARE built: crises trigger over the stocks, and elections read war weariness directly (js/power.js:576, js/elections.js).

rulings.title: a movement makes DEMANDS, they are shown on a screen of their own, and every demand gets one of three answers.
rulings.superseded_by: Completed by ruling 30 (line 2084), which says what declining and never-delivering actually do — the thing ruling 16 asserted ('never implementing makes them more angry than declining would have') without saying in what currency.
rulings.not_built: Nothing of it exists. js/movements.js has no demand, no answer and no screen; a movement's goals[] are authored flavour text (build/build_parties.py:451). This is the ruling that closes round 1's finding D and it is entirely unbuilt.

rulings.title: a grudge fades on time, there is a sixth state between Hostile and Peace, and the reunification rivalries never fade at all.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded — it is the superseding ruling, and it amends rulings 2 and 7 in place. What Wary COSTS is then set by ruling 39 (line 2526, one acceptance multiplier rather than four scaled costs) and ruling 40 (line 2561, the neighbour's movements do not grow inside you at all). Part (d)'s permanent floor is given its claimant lists by ruling 32.
rulings.not_built: No clock, no Wary and no floor in js/. NAMING: Aaron wrote 'weary' and the document renames it Wary at line 1176, because war weariness already owns that word as one of the five power stocks (js/power.js:576). That rename is one word and has not been put back to him.

rulings.title: Hostile honours what is signed and permits nothing new.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. Completed by ruling 39 (line 2526), which fills the missing middle rung — Hostile is a door that is shut, Wary a door that sticks, Peace a door that opens. The trace at line 2718 records that ruling 18's protection is empty AFTER a war, because a war has already broken every deal, so its real work is in quarrels that never become wars.
rulings.not_built: No hostile state to gate signing. The trade deal it protects is built with 2/4/8/20-turn terms (A1), which is what gives ruling 18 its free second meaning: a long deal is insurance against a relationship going bad (C94, line 1319).

rulings.title: Austin is the legitimate Texas, and the other four are rebels.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. Recorded at line 1418 as a DELIBERATE DEPARTURE from the scenario's stated principle that 'the relations board starts quiet and the player watches it sour' — flagged expressly so nobody later reads the departure as a bug. Whether conquering Austin ends the veto or makes the rebels pariahs for good is C100, open and handed to round 5.
rulings.not_built: content/scenario-shattered.json seeds no recognition at all and its relations note says the board starts quiet — verified this session. Recognition itself IS built and directed (js/recognition.js, DESIGN.md §6.5), including the measured fact this ruling turns on: the parent state's signature is worth more than every other route to recognition combined.

rulings.title: a corridor behaves under hostility exactly as a trade deal does.

rulings.title: the cost of a war belongs to the economy of war; and an Area under attack produces nothing that turn, whether or not it falls.

rulings.not_built: Not built. The mask it needs sits on data that exists: output is held per Area as a six-element sector vector across 1,688 Areas (data/economy.json), so switching an Area off denies a NAMED KIND of production — food, or the thing that moves everything else — rather than generic income. That is the round's own verification at line 1690; I did not re-measure the 1,688 figure this session.

rulings.not_built: THE CODE DISAGREES, TODAY. js/tunables.js still carries annex.budgetAreas = 3 (line 958) and annex.cooldownTurns = 4 (line 983), and js/moves.js reads both (lines 1043 and 133). Verified this session. Nothing has been changed — a design round writes documents only.

rulings.title: the four-times-your-size shield is removed.

rulings.not_built: THE CODE DISAGREES, TODAY. js/tunables.js:973 annex.strongNeighbourFactor = 4, read by js/moves.js at lines 1013 and 1060, and its own doc reads 'A neighbour this many times your size on BOTH population and GDP cannot be attacked.' Verified this session.

rulings.title: occupied ground eventually becomes your country, and how fast depends on whether life got better.

rulings.title: Allied is taken now and kept thin; Subject is deferred; and the soldiers you lend are a lever you set.

Subject is deferred to round 5 and the reason is recorded at line 1929: every nation gets one action a turn, and a subject that keeps its action is not subject while one that loses it leaves a player with no game to play.

rulings.title: a nation may declare war straight from Peace, and the reason is the whole ladder.
rulings.not_built: No declaration in js/. rulings.title: declining makes a movement grow; stringing it along makes it want something else.
rulings.superseded_by: Not superseded. rulings.not_built: THE ONE PIECE OF NEW MACHINERY THE ROUND ASKS FOR. C120 at line 2103: nothing in the built game ever changes a movement's verb. rulings.not_built: No cease-fire in js/.

rulings.title: tabling a treaty is free, and C116 is amended.

rulings.not_built: No cease-fire in js/. The principle it protects is built and load-bearing elsewhere: DESIGN.md records that answering a full-screen card does not use your turn.

rulings.title: inherited hostility travels exactly one hop.

SETTLED INTERNALLY at line 2447 — Aaron's own traced example was miscounted by one pair, reading (a) was recommended, and he agreed ('Agree with your recomendation'), so Nevada and Idaho ARE Hostile and his example needs one word. rulings.not_built: No alliances and no inheritance in js/.

rulings.not_built: No alliances and no cooling clock in js/.

rulings.title: Ruling 17 — What decides the answer: their appetite, your weight, and the relationship as a gate
rulings.not_built: Not built as a decision, though every term it reads exists — affinity, Authority, Influence and the relationship are all live in the model. Its visibility question (can a player see a neighbour's Authority and Influence?) was deferred by Aaron on 11 September, filed with C130.

rulings.not_built: Not built. Traced at the close (line 2657 onward) and found not to be a cascade — round 2's one-hop hostility is widened, not deepened — but finding J flags the opposite risk as the federation's largest balance question and an alpha watch item.

rulings.not_built: Not built. The round-2 peace machinery it preserves — both sides table terms blind and the defender chooses — is itself a design, not code.

rulings.title: Ruling 36 — The outside 15% splits evenly, and that is what buys the small nations
rulings.not_built: Not built. It also carries a default taken rather than asked — if the leader is conquered or leaves, the members hold an election immediately — which answers ruling 25's sixth question and is one line to reverse.

rulings.title: Ruling 37 — A federation trades authority for influence, and the model already computes both
rulings.not_built: Not built as an act, though both stocks it moves are built (DESIGN.md §4.1, js/power.js) and Influence already counts Reach. Its irony — that joining makes your own future unions harder — was traced at the close and resolved into a funnel rather than a trap.

rulings.title: Ruling 38 — The fervour of a new country is a tolerance, and it ends worse than neutral
rulings.not_built: Half built: the honeymoon exists as four turns of borrowed Authority against a GDP cut (js/game.js, js/power.js, js/world.js, js/scenario.js, js/tunables.js, verified this run). The tolerance applied to grievance and the fade below baseline are NOT built, and how far below and for how long were deferred, not invented.

rulings.title: Ruling 39 — A vassal keeps its own government, and its people blame that government
rulings.not_built: Not built: measured this run, 'vassal' appears in js/ only in js/tunables.js and js/victory.js, and in both places only to say a vassal contract was deliberately never invented because the save format has nowhere to put one. What submission IS stays round 5's.

rulings.title: Ruling 40 — Three words for three things: ideology, party, movement
rulings.not_built: Not built. Today one word does both jobs — content/ideologies.json names six 'ideologies' that are simultaneously the positions and the parties a nation governs as, verified this run. The change-course pricing this ruling hands to geometry is currently a treasury cost scaled by axis distance plus an Authority hit (DESIGN.md §7.4).

rulings.title: Ruling 41 — The three capped-out separatists get a ceiling above the line
rulings.not_built: EXPLICITLY SPECIFIED AND NOT MADE — the ruling says so itself: 'The change, specified exactly, and NOT made here'. Measured against data/parties.json this run, all three still read growthCap 0.35: Sagebrush Rebellion, Acadiana and El Paso United. The ruling asks for 0.45. This is live work for whoever builds next.
